title: Follow-Up: Interventions That Raise Opus 4.5 Course-Correction Above 10%

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct practical value: finding cheap, deployable interventions that raise course-correction rates would be immediately useful. The 10% baseline is strikingly low (Haiku 4.5 at 37% shows the ceiling is much higher), and demonstrating that prompt-level interventions can close the gap has clear deployment implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Lightweight prompt-level interventions (self-review instructions, opposite-consideration nudges) are easy to design and test. API-based, no model internals needed. Beginners can implement this as a structured A/B testing exercise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 6-8 interventions each tested against the full pressure battery. The combinatorial space (interventions x pressure types) is substantial. Achievable in 30 hours if the pressure battery is short (5-10 items) and interventions are tested sequentially, but tight.
